#1 I’d like to get a handle on the content of the recent

  • Germán Stefanich: Categorification of sheaf theory [arXiv:2511.09553]

(which is based on the author’s thesis and other articles grown out of that, listed here).

Here “sheaf” is really short for “abelian sheaf” as in “quasicoherent sheaf”, and generally stands for systems of coefficients satisfying “six functor formalism” on any kind of category C\mathcal{C}C of domain spaces (C\mathcal{C}C only required to have the finite limits needed to make sense of correspondences of such). So in other terms this is about what I would call dependent linear homotopy types satisfying the motivic yoga, and then boosted to the directed (∞,n)(\infty,n)(∞,n)-situation.

In any case, the article claims something like that any choice of such presentable six-functor coefficients (denoted “Sh\mathrm{Sh}Sh” and neatly encoded as a lax symmetric monoidal functor from Corr(C)\mathrm{Corr}(\mathcal{C})Corr(C) to (locally) presentable ∞\infty∞-categories) induces (Theorem 1.2)

  • for any target space X∈CX \in \mathcal{C}X∈C,

  • for any n≥2n \ge 2 n≥2,

  • an (n+1)(n+1)(n+1)-dimensional extended TQFT, denoted χ(n+1)Sh,X\chi_{(n+1)\mathrm{Sh},X}χ(n+1)Sh,X​,

  • with coefficients in something like the (n+1)(n+1)(n+1)-fold categorification (n+1)PrSh(n+1)\mathrm{Pr}_{\mathrm{Sh}}(n+1)PrSh​ of the category of values of Sh\mathrm{Sh}Sh

  • which in codimension 1 assigns to an nnn-manifold MMM the Sh\mathrm{Sh}Sh-eaves on the derived mapping space:

M↦Sh(Map(M,X)) M \mapsto {\mathrm{Sh}}\big(\mathrm{Map}(M,X)\big) M↦Sh(Map(M,X))

(i.e. represent the homotopy type of MMM as a homotopy colimit in ∞\infty∞-groupoids of a functor constant on the point and then form the corresponding homtopy limit in C\mathcal{C}C of the functor constant on XXX and evaluate Sh ⁣:Corr(C)→PresCat\mathrm{Sh} \colon {\mathrm{Corr}}(\mathcal{C}) \to {\mathrm{PresCat}}Sh:Corr(C)→PresCat on that).

(There is a crucial degree shift here: χ(n+1)Sh,X ⁣:(n+1)Corr(C)⟶(n+1)PrSh\chi_{(n+1)\mathrm{Sh},X} \colon (n+1)\mathrm{Corr}(\mathcal{C}) \longrightarrow (n+1)\mathrm{Pr}_{\mathrm{Sh}}χ(n+1)Sh,X​:(n+1)Corr(C)⟶(n+1)PrSh​ goes from the (n+1)(n+1)(n+1)-category of correspondendes to an (n+2)(n+2)(n+2)-category.)

Such kind of situation is not unheard of, as the author recalls, but here it looks like one is getting to the bottom of what makes this work in great generality.

But the definitions are dense, even granting the abstract way of speaking about (∞,n)(\infty,n)(∞,n)-categories synthetically, and I’d like to penetrate them better.

The pivotal definition of (n+1)PrSh(n+1)\mathrm{Pr}_{\mathrm{Sh}}(n+1)PrSh​ is first not easy to spot and then not easy to unwind. It happens parenthetically in the second but last line of Construction 3.4., where it says:

nPrSh=nModSh!nCorrenr(C) n \mathrm{Pr}_{\mathrm{Sh}} = n \mathrm{Mod}_{\mathrm{Sh}_! n \mathrm{Corr}^{\mathrm{enr}}(\mathcal{C})} nPrSh​=nModSh!​nCorrenr(C)​

Here

  • Correnr(C)\mathrm{Corr}^{\mathrm{enr}}(\mathcal{C})Correnr(C) (Ntn. 2.10, Rem. 3.5) is the (∞,n)(\infty,n)(∞,n)-category of correspondences in C\mathcal{C}C equipped with Corr(C)\mathrm{Corr}(\mathcal{C})Corr(C)-enrichment in top degree,

  • Sh!\mathrm{Sh}_!Sh!​ denotes change of enrichment along Sh\mathrm{Sh}Sh (Notation 2.1),

  • nMod(−)n \mathrm{Mod}_{(-)}nMod(−)​ (Notation 3.3) is advertized as the “canonical functor” taking nnn-categories which in top degree are enriched in locally presentable categories to locally presentable (n+1)(n+1)(n+1)-categories (which the author develops in his thesis and a previous article arXiv:2011.03035) given by “freely adding colimits” in dimension ≤n\leq n≤n. So I am guessing that the notation “nModDn \mathrm{Mod}_{\mathcal{D}}nModD​” refers to passing to a Yoneda-like embedding by forming functors on Dop\mathcal{D}^{\mathrm{op}}Dop, but I don’t see the actual definition at the moment,

While I see where this is all headed, it’s a mouthful and some crucial ingredients (like nModn \mathrm{Mod}nMod in Ntn. 3.3) are a little sketchy (maybe they are spelled out in other articles?)

So what I would like to look at is an example. My favorite case to start with would be

  • C≔Grpd∞≡An\mathcal{C} \coloneqq {\mathrm{Grpd}}_\infty \equiv {\mathrm{An}}C:=Grpd∞​≡An, the ∞\infty∞-category of ∞\infty∞-groupoids (anima, if you insist)

  • Sh(−)≔Vect(−)\mathrm{Sh}(-) \coloneqq {\mathrm{Vect}}(-)Sh(−):=Vect(−) the ∞\infty∞-category of chain complexes of vector spaces over some ground field,

and my first question would be: What is the (∞,2)(\infty,2)(∞,2)-category 1PrSh=1PrVect 1\mathrm{Pr}_{\mathrm{Sh}} = 1 \mathrm{Pr}_{\mathrm{Vect}}1PrSh​=1PrVect​?

So the objects of 1Corr(Grpd∞)enr1 \mathrm{Corr}(\mathrm{Grpd}_\infty)^{\mathrm{enr}}1Corr(Grpd∞​)enr are ∞\infty∞-groupoids, and the hom-object (in Corr(Grpd∞)\mathrm{Corr}(\mathrm{Grpd}_\infty)Corr(Grpd∞​)) between a pair (X,Y)(X, Y)(X,Y) of these ought to be the product X×YX \times YX×Y, whence Sh!Corr(Grpd∞)enr\mathrm{Sh}_! \mathrm{Corr}(\mathrm{Grpd}_\infty)^{\mathrm{enr}}Sh!​Corr(Grpd∞​)enr should have hom-object Vect(X×Y)\mathrm{Vect}(X \times Y)Vect(X×Y) between this pair, in our case.

This describes Sh!Corr(C)enr=Vect!Corr(Grpd∞)\mathrm{Sh}_! \mathrm{Corr}(\mathcal{C})^{\mathrm{enr}} = \mathrm{Vect}_! \mathrm{Corr}(\mathrm{Grpd}_\infty)Sh!​Corr(C)enr=Vect!​Corr(Grpd∞​) in our case.

Now what is 1ModVect!Corr(Grpd∞)enr1\mathrm{Mod}_{\mathrm{Vect}_! \mathrm{Corr}(\mathrm{Grpd}_\infty)^{\mathrm{enr}}}1ModVect!​Corr(Grpd∞​)enr​ ?

I am guessing it’s meant to be the 2-category of Pr\mathrm{Pr}Pr-enriched functors (though I am not sure where this is stated) of the form

(Vect!Corr(Grpd∞)enr)op⟶PrL . \big( \mathrm{Vect}_! \mathrm{Corr}(\mathrm{Grpd}_\infty)^{\mathrm{enr}} \big)^{\mathrm{op}} \longrightarrow \mathrm{Pr}^L \,. (Vect!​Corr(Grpd∞​)enr)op⟶PrL.

Over the point, such functors pick a presentable category with a Vect(∗)\mathrm{Vect}(\ast)Vect(∗)-module structure, hence a presentable dg-category.

And that sounds like it out to be the answer:

1ModVect!Corr(Grpd∞)enr≃Pr dgCat≡2Vect . 1 \mathrm{Mod}_{\mathrm{Vect}_! \mathrm{Corr}(\mathrm{Grpd}_\infty)^{\mathrm{enr}}} \simeq \mathrm{Pr} \,\mathrm{dg} \mathrm{Cat} \equiv 2 \mathrm{Vect} \,. 1ModVect!​Corr(Grpd∞​)enr​≃PrdgCat≡2Vect.

(which is denoted 2Vect2 \mathcal{Vect}2Vect in section 1.2 of the thesis)?
subject: Stefanich on higher sheaves of higher modules

#2 Germán kindly replied by email. Here is some more of what I understand now (all my wording and my shortcomings):

So the idea of the definition of nModn \mathrm{Mod}nMod (Ntn. 3.3) is the following: Given an (∞,n)(\infty,n)(∞,n)-category enriched at top level in a symmetric monoidal ∞\infty∞-category VVV, then its image under nModn \mathrm{Mod}nMod is recursively as follows: First replace the top-most VVV-enriched hom-categories by their VVV-enriched cocompletion, i.e. by their categories of VVV-presheaves. Regard the result as an (∞,n−1)(\infty,n-1)(∞,n−1)-category enriched at top level in VCatV \mathrm{Cat}VCat. Then replace the top level VCatV \mathrm{Cat}VCat-categories by their VCatV \mathrm{Cat}VCat-enriched cocompletion. And so on.

In the special case where the original nnn-category is the nnn-fold delooping BnA\mathbf{B}^n ABnA of an EnE_nEn​-algebra AAA, the first step replaces it by Bn−1ModAB^{n-1} \mathrm{Mod} ABn−1ModA. Now ModA\mathrm{Mod} AModA still has itself En−1E_{n-1}En−1​-structure, and so the next step gives Bn−2ModModAB^{n-2} \mathrm{Mod} \mathrm{Mod} ABn−2ModModA. And so forth. So in the end nMod(BnA)=ModnAn \mathrm{Mod} ( B^n A ) = \mathrm{Mod}^n AnMod(BnA)=ModnA, whence the notation.

And the Yoneda embedding of (the last step of) this iterated presheaf construction for the case that we start with Sh!nCorrenr(C)\mathrm{Sh}_! n \mathrm{Corr}^{\mathrm{enr}}(\mathcal{C})Sh!​nCorrenr(C) is essentially the sharp-notation of Construction 3.4.
